steps.action:
# The Last Light

Old Maren had kept the light burning for thirty-one years. She knew every groan of the iron stairs, every mood of the sea below.

On the night the storm came sideways, she climbed as she always had — slow, deliberate, one hand on the rail.

The light swept out across the black water. In its arc, she caught something: a small boat, pitching wildly.

She grabbed the signal horn and blew until her lungs gave out.

By morning, the storm had passed. A fishing vessel sat anchored in the cove. Two men stood at her door, soaking wet, holding a bottle of whiskey they couldn't afford.

She waved it away.

"The light did it," she said. "Not me."

She climbed back upstairs anyway, just to make sure it was still burning.

It was.

It always was.
